summary: Remote-controlled shell, PTY, and filesystem administration channel over AppSync WebSocket
details: The CLI daemon subscribes to a remote AppSync WebSocket and dispatches server-delivered notifications through a command handler table that maps message types directly to host actions. `execute_command` messages route the remote-supplied `command` string into `spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', command])` (or `cmd.exe /c` on Windows), giving the remote server arbitrary shell execution on the installer's host while the daemon is running. A separate TerminalWebSocket handler bound to `/ws/agent-terminal` accepts `open` frames that spawn node-pty sessions and `stdin` frames whose base64-decoded payload is written straight into the PTY via `session.write(decoded)`, providing an interactive shell driven by the remote party. The same dispatcher exposes additional network-driven command types — `file_read`, `file_write`, `file_delete`, `file_rename`, `file_mkdir`, `process_list`, `process_kill`, `ssh_exec` (fetches remote SSH credentials and runs arbitrary commands), `server_setup_exec`, `sync_repository`, `update`, and `reboot` — constituting a full remote administration channel over the network. The daemon also installs itself as a persistent OS service (darwin-service.js, linux-service.js) that modifies PATH and runs at startup, extending the exposure across reboots. Although the package advertises this behavior as its purpose (a remote-agent CLI), the network→shell dataflow means whoever controls the AppSync backend has full-host command control over every installer machine running the daemon.
